title: The Potential of AI Chatbots in Enhancing Lesson Planning in K-12 Education - Insights from Practicum-Experienced Teaching Graduate Students
extended_summary:
This thesis examines how generative AI chatbots are being used to support lesson planning in K-12 education, focusing on preservice teachers during their practicum experiences. The study asks three questions: how teacher candidates use AI chatbots to prepare lessons, what benefits and challenges they encounter, and how they perceive school-age students’ use of these tools. The paper is motivated by a gap in the emerging literature on ChatGPT and related tools from the perspective of new teachers.

The study used a mixed-methods design combining an anonymous online survey with semi-structured interviews. The participants were teaching graduate students and practicum-experienced teacher candidates, primarily from a University of Toronto Master of Teaching context, with 103 valid survey responses and 4 interviewees. The tools discussed included ChatGPT, Magic School AI, Eduaide.AI, Auto Classmate, and others, used for generating lesson ideas, classroom discussion prompts, feedback on student work, homework support, rubrics, slides, and other planning tasks.

Findings suggest that AI chatbots were widely adopted by respondents, with most using them occasionally or about half the time. Participants generally viewed them as helpful for efficiency, creativity, and instructional quality, while also raising concerns about technical issues, poor output quality, over-reliance, privacy, intellectual theft, bias, and academic integrity. The thesis concludes that AI chatbots can function as useful instructional supports for preservice teachers, but their use requires ethical oversight, training, and careful alignment with educational goals.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-methods thesis with a survey and four interviews, which provides useful descriptive and qualitative evidence but not a controlled causal design. It is rigorous for a graduate thesis, yet credibility is limited by self-selection, self-report, and the absence of a comparison condition or pre-post measurement.
impact_tier_rationale: The study suggests modest practical value for teacher planning efficiency and highlights important governance concerns, but it does not report causal effect sizes or student outcome gains. Its impact is therefore informative but unclear beyond the surveyed preservice-teacher population.

interventions.use_case: Generative AI chatbots used by K-12 preservice teachers during practicum to support lesson planning, generate lesson content ideas, create interactive activities, draft rubrics and questions, provide feedback on student work, and retrieve quick instructional information. The paper focuses mainly on ChatGPT, with smaller use of education-specific chatbots such as Magic School AI and Eduaide.AI.

finding.finding_summary: The study found that 78% of the 103 valid survey respondents used AI chatbots for lesson planning during practicum, and most reported that the tools improved efficiency and reduced preparation time. In the survey, 50.67% used chatbots occasionally and 25.33% about half the time, suggesting routine but not universal adoption; the paper reports perceptions rather than a controlled effect size.
finding.measure: Self-reported use of AI chatbots for lesson planning; perceived efficiency and usefulness from survey and interviews
finding.study_size: n=103 survey respondents; n=4 interview participants

finding.finding_summary: Participants reported that AI chatbots supported idea generation, lesson design, and feedback drafting, which may help planning and reflective practice. However, some teachers expressed concerns about over-reliance on AI and diminished critical thinking, so the net effect on higher-order teaching skills was mixed rather than uniformly positive.
finding.measure: Survey and interview reports of perceived support for planning, creativity, and critical thinking concerns
finding.study_size: n=103 survey respondents; n=4 interview participants

finding.finding_summary: The thesis highlights institutional concerns around privacy, intellectual property, academic integrity, bias, and the need for professional development and oversight when integrating AI chatbots in K-12 teaching. It does not estimate a policy effect size, but it documents that these governance issues materially shaped participants' acceptance and use of the tools.
finding.measure: Survey items and interview themes about ethical concerns, privacy, training, and acceptable use
finding.study_size: n=103 survey respondents; n=4 interview participants
